def solve(g):
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0]); out=[row[:] for row in g]
    seen=[[False]*W for _ in range(H)]
    # find connected groups of same color (non-bg), group into lines per direction, extend blocked-only... implement: for each cell, scan in all 8 dirs for maximal straight run of >=2 same-color, then walk further while background
    dirs=[(-1,0),(1,0),(0,-1),(0,1)]
    for r in range(H):
        for c in range(W):
            v=g[r][c]
            if v==1 or seen[r][c]: continue
            seen[r][c]=True
            for dr,dc in dirs:
                d=[v]*(H+W)  # placeholder
                # max run starting at (r,c)
                x,y=r,c
                run=[]
                while 0<=x<H and 0<=y<W and g[x][y]==v:
                    run.append((x,y)); x+=dr; y+=dc
                if len(run)<2: continue
                # extend from run end opposite start dir
                x,y=run[-1]; step=(dr,dc)
                added=True
                while True:
                    nrow,ncol=x+step[0],y+step[1]
                    if not(0<=nrow<H and 0<=ncol<W) or g[nrow][ncol]!=1: added=False; break
                    out[nrow][ncol]=v; x=nrow; y=ncol
                if added:
                    for rr,cc in run: seen[rr][cc]=True
                    break
    return out

# Rule refinement hypothesis: extend every diagonal run (>=2 same-color collinear diagonal cells)
# fully along its line until blocked by non-background or edge, in BOTH directions.
def solve(g,bg):
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0]); out=[row[:] for row in g]; seen=[[False]*W for _ in range(H)]
    for r in range(H):
        for c in range(W):
            v=g[r][c]
            if v==bg or seen[r][c]: continue
            # scan for maximal diagonal run starting here in either diag direction
            for dr,dc in [(1,1),(1,-1)]:
                x,y=r,c; run=[]
                while 0<=x<H and 0<=y<W and g[x][y]==v:
                    run.append((x,y)); x+=dr; y+=dc
                if len(run)<2: continue
                start=(run[-1][0]-dr,run[-1][1]-dc); end=run[0]
                ends=[(start[0],start[1]),(end[0],end[1])]
                for p in ends:
                    nr,nc=p[0]+dr,p[1]+dc
                    while 0<=nr<H and 0<=nc<W and g[nr][nc]==bg:
                        out[nr][nc]=v; nr+=dr; nc+=dc
                for rr,cc in run: seen[rr][cc]=True
    return out

d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])

    k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
    rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
    if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
        G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]

# Geometry analysis of demo3: the extension is a straight diagonal starting from (2,13) going down-left.

The direction (1,-1) passes through these 7s and beyond. So rule: continue the diagonal line that contains >=2 same-color diagonal neighbors, extending past both ends until blocked? For p3 run of 7: (1,14),(1,15)? not diagonal... (1,14) and (2,13) ARE diagonal ((1,-1)). Extension from (2,13) down-left. And up-right from (1,14) would be (0,15)=5 which blocks — consistent with "extend until non-background".
# Check p4: 8 run: (10,14),(11,15) diagonal ((1,1)); extend both ways: up-right adds (9,13)...(0,4) ✓; down-left from (11,15): (12,16)=6 → blocked ✓. 2 run: (12,15),(13,14); down-left from (13,14): (14,13)..(20,7) ✓; up-right from (12,15): (11,16)=5 blocked ✓. All other singletons stay. PERFECT.
# Implement: maximal diagonal runs (both diag dirs) length>=2 of same color; extend both ways while next cell is bg.

def f(g):
    g=[row[:] for row in g]; H=len(g); W=len(g[0])
    out=[row[:] for row in g]
    done=set()
    for rr in range(H):
        for cc in range(W):
            if (rr,cc) in done or g[rr][cc]==0: continue
            v=g[rr][cc]
            for dr,dc in ((1,1),(1,-1)):
                # check if this is part of a run continuing in +dir
                # grow run
                r,c=(rr,cc)
                prev=True
                while True:
                    nr,nc=r-dr,c-dc
                    if not(0<=nr<H and 0<=nc<W) or g[nr][nc]!=v:
                        prev=False;break
                    r,c=(nr,nc)
                r,c=(rr,cc)
                nxt=True
                while True:
                    nr,nc=r+dr,c+dc
                    if not(0<=nr<H and 0<=nc<W) or g[nr][nc]!=v: break
                    r,c=(nr,nc)
                if not nxt or prev: continue
                cells=list(range(rr,)) # placeholder
                cells=[]
                q=c
                while nxt:
                    pass
                # redo simply: collect contiguous run including (rr,cc)
                q,c0=rr-1*0,None
                cells=[]; r,c=(rr,cc)
                while True:
                    nr,nc=r+dr,c+dc
                    if not(0<=nr<H and 0<=nc<W) or g[nr][nc]!=v: break
                    r,c=(nr,nc); cells.append((nr,nc))
                start_r,start_c=rr,cc
                while True:
                    nr,nc=start_r-dr,start_c-dc
                    if not(0<=nr<H and 0<=nc<W) or g[nr][nc]!=v: break
                    start_r,start_c=nr,nc
                cells=[(start_r,start_c)]+cells
                if len(cells)<2: continue
                for step in ((dr,dc),(-dr,-dc)):
                    # extend from end cell
                    r,c = cells[-1] if step==(dr,dc) else cells[0]
                    r2,c2=(r+step[0],c+step[1])
                    while 0<=r2<H and 0<=c2<W and g[r2][c2]==0:
                        out[r2][c2]=v; r2+=step[0]; c2+=step[1]
                done.update(cells)
    return out
print('p3', f(G['Demo pair 3 input'])==G['Demo pair 3 output'], 'p4', f(G['Demo pair 4 input'])==G['Demo pair 4 output'])
